\noindent\tcbox[we pill]{A.\enspace A valid route that bypasses milestones}

\smallskip
\noindent A mechanical-engineering question (Intermediate) gives a velocity field and asks for the
vorticity at a point:
\begin{tcolorbox}[we module, colback=weModule]
A 2D fluid flow is described by the velocity field:\\[3pt]
\hspace*{1.5em}u = -1xy\\[1pt]
\hspace*{1.5em}v = 1x\^{}2 - 2y\^{}2\\[3pt]
where u and v are in m/s, and x and y are in meters.\\[3pt]
Calculate the vorticity at the point (1.3, 1.1) m and determine if the flow is rotational or
irrotational at that point.
\end{tcolorbox}
\begin{tcolorbox}[we module, colback=white]
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.3}
\begin{tabular*}{\linewidth}{@{\extracolsep{\fill}}l r l l@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Milestone} & \textbf{Gold value} & \textbf{Settled by} & \textbf{Outcome} \\
\midrule
\texttt{du\_dy\_val} & $-1.3$ & judge & not needed \\
\texttt{dv\_dx\_val} & $2.6$ & judge & not needed \\
\texttt{zeta\_z} & $3.9$ & matching & states $3.9$, $c = 1$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular*}
\end{tcolorbox}
\noindent The gold trace evaluates the two partial derivatives at the point; the response
differentiates symbolically, $\omega_z = 2x - (-x) = 3x$, and evaluates $3(1.3) = 3.9$ in one step,
so it never states \texttt{du\_dy\_val} and \texttt{dv\_dx\_val}. The answer is correct, $v(r) = 1$;
MC credits only reached, so $m(r) = 1/3$, and route-adjusted coverage, with the not-needed
milestones out of the denominator, is 1/1.
